reason: The cited evidence (E1) reports mass loss and elemental depletion in an FCC HEA vs. 316H stainless steel in FLiBe salt, but it does not address Q235 steel, native iron-oxide scales, phase transformations, or spallation mechanisms. None of the key premises about oxide stability, phase transitions, or protection mechanisms are supported by this passage.
premises: Native iron-oxide scale on Q235 steel can be protective (magnetite/spinel) or non-protective (hematite) depending on temperature.
High temperature (700–900 °C) can trigger phase transformation or spallation of the oxide scale.
Oxide scale stability and adherence control the transition from corrosion protection to degradation.
Mass change and oxide characterization can distinguish protective vs. non-protective behavior.
